integrity: Equality in the source radial growth bound forces the odd Koebe square-root combination and the positive quadratic analytic dilatation. The resulting shear is locally orientation-preserving but explicitly noninjective, as shown by real-part variation at paired sides of the two vertical slits. Compactness of the univalent family yields a strictly smaller achieved best constant. An exact analytic proof, rather than only sampled collisions, establishes the classification.
scientific_limitations: The result proves a strict, attained-bound gap for each fixed positive radius and positive dilatation parameter but gives no explicit formula or uniform quantitative lower bound for that gap. It applies only to normalized odd harmonic univalent mappings possessing an analytic univalent combination.
title: Strict growth gap from global univalence in odd quasiconformal harmonic maps
